RFC8654-3-1.note: Independent whole-composition rejudgment, 2026-10-09, after the direct change to TestRFC8654TreatAsWithdrawRemovesInstalledRoutes. RFC 8654 Section 3, rfc/full/rfc8654.txt:109-110: 'Peers that wish to use the BGP Extended Message Capability MUST support error handling for BGP UPDATE messages per [RFC7606].' This retains the prior composed receive-error-handling judgment, not a substitution of one ORIGIN case for all RFC 7606 obligations. Read the covering extended-message and forward-handle architecture documents, the unqualified summary row and derived ledger, the prior canonical composition, all eight distinct tagged test functions (fourteen tag carriers), the common classification/enforcement/synthesis producers, and the relevant RIB publication producers. No partial, gap or single-polarity annotation narrows this row. Obligation: RFC 7606 Section 2 requires actual removal of every contained route from Adj-RIB-In, not suppression of the malformed UPDATE; Section 7.1 says 'An UPDATE message with a malformed ORIGIN attribute SHALL be handled using the approach of treat-as-withdraw.' The changed test first installs both prefixes from an exactly 4097-octet UPDATE into real source storage and Loc-RIB and observes downstream announcements. It changes only ORIGIN to 3, then requires both routes absent from actual storage and Loc-RIB and both withdrawals on recipient TCP while retaining the source peer storage. Recovery reuses the same 4097-octet buffer, changing ORIGIN to 1 and MED to 17: both stored routes must contain those exact values, both prefixes must reach recipient TCP with each exact attribute, both actual Loc-RIB publications must carry Best.Metric 17, and both final selected paths must have Metric 17. Same Session identity, Established state and no source NOTIFICATION remain mandatory. Initial ORIGIN 0/MED 0 cannot satisfy the recovery assertions. Isolation/discrimination: the invalid frame is a clone differing only in ORIGIN; suppression of withdrawal, partial removal, session reset, lost recovery, stale attributes or stale selected metric fails a concrete assertion. The optional Forward handle is not an RFC obligation: rib_structured.go::handleReceivedStructured inserts routes before per-prefix election; rib_aigp.go::reselectAIGPRoutes elects stored routes with nil forward; rib_bestchange.go::checkRouteBestChange maps MED to Path.Metric; locrib/manager.go::insert does not dispatch an identical Path. This establishes a source-permitted nil-forward interleaving, not a runtime trace of that interleaving. The new oracle observes the selected-path contract without weakening the required route/wire outcomes. Whole composition retained: the structural validator pair requires exact None versus TreatAsWithdraw/COMMUNITY/Section 4; the session carrier distinguishes 1100-route withdrawal from unlocatable-section reset with exact NOTIFICATION 3/1 and zero dispatch; valid/malformed ATOMIC_AGGREGATE and AGGREGATOR controls require actual discard and continued delivery through both readers; duplicate recognized/unrecognized attributes require exact keep-first output, while duplicate MP attributes require reset and no additional dispatch; the two-family installed-route carrier requires primary and extra-family removal/recipient withdrawal, an unrelated survivor and same-session recovery. These compose with the previously reviewed clause-specific RFC 7606 controls, typed-family and ADD-PATH handling, original-message ordinary/coalesced standard/extended validation, diagnostic wire/NLRI controls, and late-first-AS/late-tunnel empty-MP versus reachable-NLRI matrices. The latter retain exact reset/Idle/connection closure/zero dispatch for errors without reachable NLRI, exact withdrawals without reset for reachable counterparts, valid-input acceptance and diagnostic silence, and exact original header-inclusive diagnostic hex. ATTR_SET and empty-MP corrections remain RFC-backed, not weakened expectations. Runtime evidence: job-rfc8654-recovery-causal-oracle-native-records-ffdb06d6.log records both renewed polarities using session_validation.go::applyRFC7606 replaced by a panic; both named broken runs fail at initial route installation. discriminate_observe.go::observationRunner.requireCleanGreen first requires the unbroken selected unit to pass and then proves producer coverage, so each successful record also establishes a clean selected-unit baseline. The halt proves dependence on applyRFC7606 only; it does not selectively discriminate recovery attributes, metric publication, withdrawal semantics, or the whole sentence. Prior accepted runtime observations remain the canonical note's late-first-AS, corrected admission and late-tunnel jobs; they are not newly rerun here. Implemented-and-tested: the composed error-action, dispatch, installed-route, wire, selected-path and diagnostic assertions above. Implemented-but-unverified by this renewal: fresh full-reactor race20 acceptance and selective recovery-semantic mutation discrimination; neither is claimed complete. No absent error-handling feature or newly unproven clause within the previously accepted receive composition was identified by this scoped rejudgment. Exact final route-owner release versus outbound admission remains the separately disclosed ownership proof gap, not established by this test or verdict; parent/child specifications, publication and remaining runtime acceptance stay open. This is not a whole-RFC conformance claim and does not absorb unrelated deterministic-audit findings or owner-approved persist retirement.

RFC8654-3-2.note: Code 6 is the whole obligation; row single-polarity positive (a fixed code has no refusal form). TestRFC8654ExtendedMessageWireIsCode6Length0 reads the octet WriteTo puts at a non-zero offset (06), Code()==6, and Parse(06 00) yields *ExtendedMessage: a code drift in WriteTo or in Parse's dispatch goes red. The old TestCapabilityCodeConstants tag (constant only) is supplementary. Judge 2026-09-30.

RFC8654-3-3.note: Positive: WriteTo writes exactly 06 00 with Len 2 and nothing beyond, Parse(06 00) accepted. Negative: TestRFC8654ExtendedMessageNonZeroLengthRefused sends code 6 with length 1 and 4 and requires ErrInvalidLength and no capability. Judge break: parseZeroLengthCapability accepting a non-zero length (len>8 guard) turned the negative red. Single-polarity marker removal is correct: a refusal path exists.

RFC8654-4-2.note: Non-compliant: an UPDATE on the wire larger than the negotiated maximum. TestSendUpdateWithSplitBoundsAnOversizePayload drives Peer.sendUpdateWithSplit with an over-4096 payload to a non-extended peer and asserts every wire frame length <= 4096 with the NLRI preserved; TestSendUpdateWithSplitTracksTheNegotiatedMaximum asserts the bound is 65535 when negotiated; BuildUnicastWithMaxSize refuses an oversize build (ErrUpdateTooLarge). Both polarities.

RFC8654-4-3.note: Prior independent judgment retained after scope comparison, not gratuitously re-audited. The complete Section 4 exception sentence and tagged units are unchanged: TestMaxMessageLength, TestValidateLengthWithMax, and TestRFC8654AdvertisementDoesNotExtendControlBounds. The directional test file gained an import and sibling accumulation unit; its control-bound unit is unchanged in the scoped diff. OPEN 4097 and KEEPALIVE 20 still require exact NOTIFICATION 1/2 in both readers, while valid controls and all supported type maxima are pinned. No new foreign execution or canonical fingerprint computation is claimed. The parent stamping tool must compute current unit/file hashes.

RFC8654-5-1.note: Independent current-source renewal. RFC8654 Section 5 (rfc/full/rfc8654.txt): "A BGP speaker that has the ability to use BGP Extended Messages but has not advertised the BGP Extended Message Capability, presumably due to configuration, MUST NOT accept a BGP Extended Message." TestRFC8654ReceiveLimitFollowsLocalOPEN exchanges actual OPENs for all four local/peer capability combinations and exercises both readers at Length 4096, 4097 and 65535. Without local advertisement it requires an error, zero consumer dispatch and exact NOTIFICATION 1/2 carrying the offending Length; local-only advertisement supplies the distinct accepting control with exact complete payload and Established continuity. Header tests independently pin rejection and permitted extended lengths. Both current FRR rejection carriers reach checkExtendedMessages and checkExtendedReceiveRejection: they distinguish Ze's original OPEN from the relay-delivered OPEN, require a real FRR oversized UPDATE, exact offending-length NOTIFICATION and closure of the original FRR session generation. Their current execution is parent-owned and is not inferred from source inspection. handleOpen derives local capabilities from the actual local OPEN; Negotiate retains local receive permission independently of peer send permission; both reader admission gates consume the receive permission before reading the body. negotiateWith now computes Negotiate under mu before taking writeMu, while pointer publication, initPathsLimit and writeBuf.Resize remain writer-locked. Prompt failure under a whole-body Negotiate panic establishes producer dependence and cleanup progress, not a semantic admission counterfactual.

RFC8654-5-4.note: Independent ReceiveWholeClauseFinal renewal: current controls assert exact NOTIFICATION 1/2 with erroneous Length 0x1001 followed by EOF, real Adj-RIB-In/Loc-RIB cleanup and resource release, actual recipient withdrawals, a valid-4096 retention control, and alternate-best replacement with exact survivor attributes, one Loc-RIB ChangeUpdate and no transient withdrawal. readAndProcessCoalesced rejects the fatal header before reading its body; handleStructuredState purges and invokes re-election outside peerMu; the RS retains detached withdrawal identities throughout its joined DOWN operation; recoverNLRIBatch waits for received-event publication and applied delivery before lookup, fences destination/source ownership at the actual writer, and receives completion after write/flush or fails closed. This ownership trace, not cross-plugin timestamp ordering, supports RFC4271 Section6 lifetime obligations. Fatal-length, valid-length, alternate-election and recovery controls pass in job-ownership-final-complete-packages-race-a95e6797.log; current full reactor/message race passes in job-receive-final-reactor-message-race-7d820229.log. Native bindings are separate proof; unchanged header-only missing bindings are standing metadata debt, not a new semantic gap.

RFC8654-6-1.note: Both Section 6 paragraphs are retained: common header minimum, the raised maximum only after local capability advertisement, and OPEN/KEEPALIVE exceptions; header controls assert per-type limits, invalid lengths, OPEN refusal above 4096 and KEEPALIVE refusal at 20, while capability tests distinguish receive and send permission for all four advertisement combinations; ReceiveLimitFollowsLocalOPEN exchanges actual OPENs and drives both readers at 4096, 4097 and 65535, requiring exact complete dispatched payloads or NOTIFICATION 1/2 with erroneous Length and no dispatch; AnnouncementAccumulation uses individually standard-sized inputs to isolate batching capacity and asserts exact consumer batches beyond 4096 through 65535, overflow/KEEPALIVE flushing and standard-sized batching without local advertisement; current source uses the directional receive permission for buffers and header admission, and existing TestValidateLengthWithMax binding omissions are standing metadata debt rather than a new source or semantic gap
